utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Neimann, any further questions you would like to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: A few short questions (Re-examined by Mr. Niemann)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W on the 24th of January, 1993, when you observed the snipers in the buildings, did you know at that time whether there were any parts of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in that area, or was it only the HVO army that was there at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: It was only the HVO, because the BH army was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were ordered to go to the centre of Busovaca, did you know of any Muslim people who were in positions of authority there at that time who would have given any such orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, I didn't move around town very much. I was too afraid for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, the person that you knew as the commander of the camp, I'll give you two names, I want you to tell me is it the first name or the second name that you understand as the person who was commander of the camp. Was it Zlatko Teloslovski, or did you understand it as Zlatko Aleksovski. The first one or the second?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Aleksovski, you know, it's hard for me to say the word, because I don't have the, all my teeth, so, I can't really say it clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why I asked you to tell me, is it the first one or the second one? Is it the first one Zlatko Teloslovski or the second one, Zlatko Aleksovski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: You know, I really have trouble saying it, but the second one, the second one. So much I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Witness W, as far as I'm concerned, I have a couple of questions for you. A little while ago, if I remember what you said well, you told us that in Busovaca you had seen soldiers bearing the HV and the HVO insignias, have I understood you right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So, my question is the following: How were you able to distinguish between the HV and the HVO insignias?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: First it was the HVO and then there was something called HOS. Those were two separate insignia, and in the end, later on, it was all HVO, later on. I saw the insignia on the arms, so that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I see, thank you very much. You also said that some soldiers wore a stocking over their face, whereas some soldiers did not wear anything over their faces.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes, they had the HVO insignia, but they had these stocking masks, with slits for the eyes so they can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Precisely. So, is it possible to establish the following distinction: The HVO soldiers wore a stocking mask, whereas the HV soldiers did not bear such a mask over their face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: The ones who were not known in the area, they did not need them, and those who were known, they would put these masks on their faces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I will quote what you have said earlier on. You said that the soldiers who wore the HV insignias did not wear a stocking mask; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: The ones who people did not know did not have the stocking mask, and those who feared that they could be recognised by people did wear them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But is it possible to establish a link between those soldiers of the HV who were not known in the area and the fact that they did not wear a stocking mask? Is it possible to establish such a link?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Ones who were not known in the area did not wear them. But those who could be recognised, those did wear them, and this is what I noticed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Another question. You told us that you did not know the doctor that you saw in Busovaca, I think it was a woman, that woman you saw in the medical centre of Busovaca, you said you did not know that woman; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, no, I did not recognise her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But were you supposed to recognise her? Would you have been able to recognise her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: None of the lady doctors who used to work there were around. There was another set of physicians who arrived. This is what I observed, including the nurses, they were also unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So, in a small city such as Busovaca, people were supposed to know the doctors working for the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Another question. You told us that you gave the doctor's prescription to Mr. Aleksovski; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: You gave him the paper directly? You gave him the paper yourself? Or did another person hand this paper over to Mr. Aleksovski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, I handed it to him directly, into his hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: You also said that the guards had driven you to the Blue 11 restaurant; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But what guards are you talking about. Are you talking about the guards who were also guards in the Kaonik camp, or those guards who were those who worked in other facilities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: That I cannot tell. I know that we were called out from our cells, one by one, to come out of the cells which were in this hangar where we were staying, and we were ordered to board the Rab vehicle, that's how it was, now, whether they were civilians or not that I was not looking at -- for who was driving it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I see. But inside the Blue 11 restaurant, you told us that the guards had electric lamps with them, and you said that they lighted those lamps and they put them on your faces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So, one can imagine that if you have a light shining in your face you can't see anything, what I mean is that you can't see the face of the person who is holding the electric lamp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: It was a flashlight which had a strong enough light, and this was shining our way to the Blue 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: If I have understood you rightly, there was no light inside the restaurant; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Very well, then. Witness W, we have no further questions for you. Your testimony before this Tribunal is now over, we thank you very much for your testimony before this Tribunal, you may now leave. We wish you a safe journey home. You may now leave, sir. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Neimann, there is no other witness for today; is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your, that is the evidence that in rebuttal that the Prosecution seeks to call.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: And Mr. Mikulicic, what about you? What are your plans?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, now that the Defence has heard what evidence the Prosecution had in rebuttal, the Defence will analyse this evidence and will offer its own rejoinder to counter the evidence produced by the Prosecution. At this point in time the Defence is unable to say which witnesses it will call, the number and the scope of their testimony, but after an analysis of the evidence offered by the Prosecution here, which will not take long, we will be able to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So, if I understood you well, you do plan to call some other witnesses. Do you have an idea when you will be able to call these witnesses to the stand? Give us an estimation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence will comply to the schedule which the Tribunal has. We will be realistic about this, and we would like to hear what the availability is of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: The Judges are always at your disposal, Mr. Mikulicic, are always ready to work. There is a schedule, there is a schedule we had agreed upon, and if I'm right, I think that October 5th was the planned date for the closing, or rather for the written submissions. I think there has been an agreement between the parties, agreement according to which these written submissions would be filed simultaneously, October 5th is the latest date. Then the week from the 12th to the 16th of October is the week during which we are planning to hold our last hearings, hearings that will enable the Prosecution to give its closing argument, which will enable also the Defence to give its closing arguments, such is the schedule as it now stands. As you well know, the Judges have always had one priority, efficiency and effectiveness, and in my name and in the name of my colleagues, I can tell you once again that the Chamber will always be happy to work and to go on with our work. In any case, we would be very happy to end this case as early as possible. So, if we speak in concrete terms, you said you wanted to call additional witnesses. You have until the 12th of October to call these witnesses to the stand. If you're able to call them before the 12th of October, then our schedule stays as it is. But if you are planning to call these witnesses after the 12th of October, then of course our schedule must be changed. Mr. Mikulicic, I have another idea. If you want to, we could take a small break. You know that we can work in this courtroom until 2.30, maybe we could take a five or ten-minute break that will give you time to think about all this, then we will resume our work for five or ten minutes in order to solve this problem. Mr. Neimann, do you agree on this proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So, a ten-minute break which will allow Mr. Mikulicic to solve the problem.
